section.title: Activity (18 minutes)
section.para: This lesson combines the skills from the first activity: using the slope formula and finding the equation of a line given a point and the slope. First, students use the slope formula to find the slope. Then, they use the point-slope formula to write the equation. Encourage students to write out an example in a notebook or on paper or notecards. The graph gives students a visual representation of slope, change in \( y \), \( {\ y}_2-y_1 \) over change in \( x \), \( x_2-x_1 \).
section.title: Launch
section.para: Consider having student work in pairs. After the self-check, suggest students graph the line with a graphing calculator or Desmos to see that the line goes through the two points. Have them check the \(y\)-intercept also.

section.title: Activity Synthesis
section.para: There are two important concepts in this lesson. Help students understand the relationship between the points on a line, the slope of the line, and the equation of the line. Students may be able to understand the slope-intercept form of the equation of the line because they can look at the graph of the line and see the \(y\)-intercept, and they can count out the slope using rise over run. Students may not see the relationship between the points on the line and the point-slope form of the equation. One way to help students see is to give them 4 equations in point-slope form: A: \(y-1=2(x+1)\); B: \(y-5=2(x-1)\); C: \(y-5=-2(x-1)\); D: \(y-1=-2(x+1)\).
Here are some things to discuss:

list.item: “Which equations go through the same points? Name the points.” (A and D go through \((-1, 1)\); B and C go through \((1, 5)\).)
“Which equations have the same slope? Name the slope.” (A and B have slope 2. C and D have slope \(-2\).)
“Do lines A and B represent the same line? Explain how you know.” (Yes; A and B represent the line \(y=2x+3\).)
“Do lines C and D represent the same line? Explain how you know.” (No; Line C represents the line \(y-2x+7\). Line D represents the line \(y=-2x-1\). They are not the same line.)

section.para: If there is time, have students graph the lines to check the responses.
section.title: 1.12.5: Self Check

para.emphasis: After the activity, students will answer the following question to check their understanding of the concepts explored in the activity.

section.para: QUESTION:
Which equation represents the slope-intercept form of the equation of a line containing the points \( (–2, –4) \) and \( (1, –3) \)?

row.entry:
That’s correct! Check yourself:
First, find the slope by substituting \( –3 \) for \( y_2 \), \( –4 \) for \( y_1 \), 1 for \( x_2 \), and \( –2 \) for \( x_1 \) in the slope formula: \( m= \frac{y_2-y_1}{x_2-x_1} \).
The slope is \( m= \frac{-3-(-4)}{1-(-2)} = \frac{1}{3} \).
Substitute the slope and the coordinates of the points into the point-slope form: \( y - y_1 = m(x - x_1) \).
Simplify the equation \( y - (-3) = \frac{1}{3}(x - 1) \) to get \( y + 3 = \frac{1}{3}x - \frac{1}{3} \).

Incorrect. Let’s try again a different way: First find the slope by substituting \( –3 \) for \( y_2 \), \( –4 \) for \( y_1 \), 1 for \( x_2 \), and \( –2 \) for \( x_1 \) in the slope formula: \( m= \frac{y_2-y_1}{x_2-x_1} \).
The slope is \( m= \frac{-3-(-4)}{1-(-2)} = \frac{1}{3} \).
Substitute the slope and the coordinates of the points into the point-slope form: \( y - y_1 = m(x - x_1) \).
You can use the coordinates from either point.
Make sure you choose the \( x \) and \( y \) value from the same point.
Simplify the equation \( y - (-3) = \frac{1}{3}(x - 1) \) to get \( y + 3 = \frac{1}{3}x - \frac{1}{3} \).
The answer is \( y =\frac{1}{3}x - 3\frac{1}{3} \).

Incorrect. Let’s try again a different way: First find the slope by substituting \( –3 \) for \( y_2 \), \( –4 \) for \( y_1 \), 1 for \( x_2 \), and \( –2 \) for \( x_1 \) in the slope formula: \( m= \frac{y^2-y1}{x^2-x1} \).
The slope is \( m= \frac{-3-(-4)}{1-(-2)} = \frac{1}{3} \).
Substitute the slope and the coordinates of the points into the point-slope form: \( y - y_1 = m(x - x_1) \).
Simplify the equation \( y - (-3) = \frac{1}{3}(x - 1) \) to get \( y + 3 = \frac{1}{3}x - \frac{1}{3} \).
The answer is \( y =\frac{1}{3}x - 3\frac{1}{3} \).

Incorrect. Let’s try again a different way: Remember, the \(x\)-coordinate is the first coordinate, and the \(y\)-coordinate is the second coordinate.
The slope is the change in \(y\) over the change in \(x\).
Find the slope by substituting \( –3 \) for \( y_2 \), \( –4 \) for \( y_1 \), 1 for \( x_2 \), and \( –2 \) for \( x_1 \) in the slope formula: \( m= \frac{y_2-y_1}{x_2-x_1} \).
The slope is \( m= \frac{-3-(-4)}{1-(-2)} = \frac{1}{3} \). Substitute the slope and the coordinates of the points into the point-slope form: \( y - y_1 = m(x - x_1) \).
Simplify the equation \( y - (-3) = \frac{1}{3}(x - 1) \) to get \( y + 3 = \frac{1}{3}x - \frac{1}{3} \).
The answer is \( y =\frac{1}{3}x - 3\frac{1}{3} \).

section.title: 1.12.5: Additional Resources
Find an Equation of the Line Given Two Points

para.emphasis: The following content is available to students who would like more support based on their experience with the self check. Students will not automatically have access to this content, so you may wish to share it with those who could benefit from it.

section.para: So far, you have two options for finding an equation of a line: slope-intercept or point-slope. When you start with two points, it makes more sense to use the point-slope form.
But then you need the slope. You can find the slope with just two points and then use it and one of the given points to find the equation.
Write the equation of a line that contains the points \( (–3, –1) \) and \( (2, –2) \). Write the equation in slope-intercept form and standard form.

Step 1 - Find the slope using the given points.
Find the slope of the line through \( (–3, –1) \) and \( (2, –2) \).
\( m = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 -x_1} \)
\( m = \frac{-2 - (-1)}{2-(-3)} \)
\( m = \frac{-1}{5} \)
\( m = - \frac{1}{5} \)

Step 2 - Choose one point.
Choose either point.
\( (x_1, y_1) \)
\( (2, –2) \)

Step 3 - Substitute the values into the point-slope form, \( y - y_1 = m(x - x_1) \).
Simplify
\( \begin{array}{rcl}y-y_1&=&m(x-x_1)\\y-(-2)&=&-\frac15(x-2)\\y+2&=&-\frac15x+\frac25\end{array} \)

Step 4 - Write the equation in slope-intercept form.
\( y = -\frac{1}{5}x - \frac{8}{5} \)

Step 5 - Convert slope-intercept form to standard form.
\(y=−\frac15x−\frac85\)
\(\frac15x+ y= −\frac85\)
\(5(\frac15x+ y)=5(−\frac85)\)
\((1x+ 5y)= −8\)

section.title: Try It: Writing the Equation of a Line Given the Slope and Point
section.para: Write the equation of a line that contains the points \( (–3, 5) \) and \( (–3, 4) \).
Write down your answer, and then select the solution button to compare your work.
section.title: Answer:
section.para: Here is how to find an equation of a line that contains the points \( (–3, 5) \) and \( (–3, 4) \).
Again, the first step will be to find the slope.
Step 1 - Find the slope of the line through \( (–3, 5) \) and \( (–3, 4) \).

A line with undefined slope is a vertical line. Both given points have an \( x \)-coordinate of \( –3 \). So, the equation of the line is \( x = -3 \). There is no \( y \), so the equation cannot be written in slope-intercept form.
